title: A one-paragraph idea turned into calls engineering can build on
before:
- Edits should show up for everyone. We do NOT have real-time collaborative editing today; notes save on blur and last write wins.
- Should invitees need Pro? Not sure. Sales wants it free for invitees to spread the product.
- Deleting a shared folder: what happens to other people's copies? Unclear.
after:
| # | Call | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | One canonical folder, **no per-member copies**. Members access the owner's folder; nothing gets duplicated. | The "what happens to other people's copies" question goes away because there are no copies. |
| D2 | **Last-write-wins is not allowed on shared notes.** Saves carry a `base_version`. A stale save becomes a **conflicted copy** next to the original, and the server does it atomically. | With several editors on blur-save, LWW silently loses meeting notes. That's the worst failure this feature can have. Real-time co-editing doesn't fit in 6 weeks. |
| D3 | "Edits show up for everyone" means **within about 30 seconds**, via refresh-on-focus plus polling. It does not mean real-time. | Meets the ask ("we all see the same notes") without a sync engine. |
…
| D7 | Deleting a shared folder **soft-deletes it for everyone**. Members are emailed. Support can restore it for 30 days. | Follows from D1. Confirmation still needed (Q2). |
caption: From the 335-line spec in docs/shared-folders-spec.md, which also covers an authorization matrix, 15 acceptance criteria, a six-week slice plan, and open questions with owners and dates.
